summary: The repo exists and is active. It is a TypeScript/React 19/Vite 8/three r183 port of the Chrono Divide browser client (the Chinese RA2WEB build), migrated module by module from the extracted JS bundle of that client. It is not an original engine. huangkaoya/redalert2 is the same repo under its old name: GitHub returns a 301 from github.com/huangkaoya/redalert2 to /ts-redalert2, and the API resolves both to repo id 989980031. Since 2026-09-03 the repo's own LICENSE says the Chrono Divide-derived code is NOT licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other license. The README body still claims GPL-3.0, so the two contradict each other. Technically it works for vanilla RA2 skirmish: a large rules.ini-driven simulation, skirmish vs a ported community bot, WebRTC LAN lockstep, replays, and a real Three.js ortho-isometric 3D scene with voxel meshes and shadow maps. It builds cleanly in under 1 second with bun. There is no campaign, no Yuri's Revenge (hard-coded to RA2), no online play (WOL is stubbed), no save/load, no map editor and no FMV cutscenes. As a legal base for a remaster it is close to disqualified, unless the user gets written permission from Chrono Divide's author (Alexandru Ciucă).
license_evidence: VERIFIED (current LICENSE file, commit 898d891, 2026-09-03, message "Revise LICENSE to reflect copyright holder's terms"). This commit replaced the full GPL-3.0 text with this notice: "This repository contains code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client. The Chrono Divide copyright holder has not licensed Chrono Divide-derived material contained in this repository. Such material is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license. GPL-3.0 applies, where indicated, solely to independently authored contributions ... No statement in this repository should be interpreted as granting rights to Chrono Divide-derived code." The GitHub API now reports license "Other"/NOASSERTION. The README contradicts this: it still says "本项目基于GNU General Public License v3.0（GPL-3.0）许可证开源" but also says all rights, including profit rights, belong to the Chrono Divide/RA2WEB owner, and it bans commercial use. No per-file headers mark any file as GPL. package.json has no "license" field and "private": true. Third-party code inside: src/game/ai/thirdpartbot/builtIn is a port of Supalosa/supalosa-chronodivide-bot. That repo has no LICENSE file and no license field in package.json (checked via gh api), so by default all rights are reserved. The repo also ships EA/Westwood-derived data files. public/ini.mix contains the original ART.INI/AI.INI, with comments like "; ART.INI ... Tiberian Sun" and "Westwood" strings. public/general.csf is a 4,480-label RA2 string table. The downstream forks (e.g. github.com/dvorovrus/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad, "Base: huangkaoya/redalert2 @ 8c07f10") write that the upstream GPL grant should be treated "as unverified rather than settled".
provenance: Derived from Chrono Divide. It is a manual and AI-assisted TypeScript migration ("decompile") of the Chrono Divide / RA2WEB client's extracted JS modules, made by someone affiliated with ra2web.com. It is not original work, and it is not a GitHub fork.

VERIFIED in repo and history:
(1) The LICENSE says "code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client".
(2) The README says it is "developed based on the analysis of the Chinese version of Chronodivide — RA2WEB", and that the Chrono Divide owner "has never open-sourced the game client code in any form".
(3) The deleted PROJECT_CONTEXT_SUMMARY.md (visible at 2247335 and 356af5f^) is titled "Project Context Summary (RA2Web React Decompile)". It says the goal is "to reverse-engineer an existing JavaScript project" whose files are in `extracted_modules_simple/` with a `module-dependencies.json`. It lists 1:1 ports such as `Base64.js -> Base64.ts` and `Application.js`, and states principles like "migrate what IS, not what 'should be'". It was deleted in commit 356af5f, "删除无用文件" ("delete useless files"), on 2025-09-07.
(4) Several bulk-dump commits: bd49b31 "core game engine" (2025-06-01) added 452 files and 41,019 lines at once. a7af43a "整理" ("tidy-up", 2026-03-16) touched 1,184 files (+89,783/−120,427).
(5) Minifier leftovers remain. src/engine/renderable/builder/vxlGeometry/VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder.ts is literally minified code (`var a=(s+1)%3,n=(s+2)%3,o=new Int32Array(3)...`, `j=!1`). There are about 270 `(e, t)`-style parameter lists (e.g. TriggerConditionFactory.create(e: any, t: any)), about 7,000 `any` uses, and 24 stub classes typed `[key: string]: any`.
(6) Chrono Divide identifiers are still present: public/servers.ini points to wss://wol-eu1.chronodivide.com. GameLoader.ts loads '@chronodivide/sp-bots' via SystemJS. game-api.ts is a "Local shim for @chronodivide/game-api". The locale disclaimer reads '"Chrono Divide" is a non-profit fan project'. The credits say "原项目开发 Chronodivide" ("original project developer: Chronodivide"). config.ini points to download.ra2web.com.
(7) The owner's other GitHub repos are forks of the ra2web org: ra2web/ra2web-proxy ("forwards the official Chronodivide client and dynamically injects code and content"), ra2web/ra2web.github.io ("chronodivide assets") and ra2web/.github ("integrates the Chronodivide open-source parts").
(8) In issue #39 the owner says the project "是基于RA2WEB.com 的分析，并不是从头构思撰写" ("based on analysis of RA2WEB.com, not conceived and written from scratch") and "原项目不是开源项目" ("the original project is not open source").
Related candidates (VERIFIED via gh api): OpenRA2/RA2Web and DD-Channel/ra2-web are GitHub forks of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, so they carry the same problem. The RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad repos (ammaarreshi, dvorovrus, john-overton, etc.) are based on huangkaoya/redalert2@8c07f10. ra2-games/ra2 (created 2026-09-12, 238 stars) is not a GitHub fork and claims GPL-3.0-or-later; I did not verify its lineage here. External: chronodivide.com calls itself a fan project and publishes no client source. The chronodivide GitHub org only holds mod-sdk, game-api-playground and pvpgn-server (https://github.com/chronodivide). Author: Alexandru Ciucă (https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3502012310166400).
tech_stack: TypeScript 5.9.3 with strict:false and noImplicitAny:false. React 19.2.4. Vite 8.0.1 (rolldown). Bun 1.3.x as package manager (bun.lock, with a package-lock.json also present). three 0.183.2 (WebGLRenderer, which is WebGL2-only in this version). shader-particle-engine 1.0.6, patched for r183 in src/engine/renderable/fx/speCompat.ts. three.meshline. @brakebein/threeoctree. 7z-wasm for importing archives. @ffmpeg/ffmpeg (wasm) for BIK→WebM. file-system-access polyfill (OPFS/FS Access API). mersenne-twister (PRNG). @ra2web/pcxfile and @ra2web/wavefile. qrcode/jsqr for LAN SDP exchange. Playwright is a devDependency, but the scripts/ folder is gitignored and missing (open issue #53). Size: 1,271 files in src, about 128.7k lines of TS/TSX. By area: game 44k, gui 35.6k, engine 24.7k, tools 9.3k, data 6.1k, network 4.5k.
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED in code.
Entry and structure: src/main.tsx → App.tsx → Application.ts → Gui.ts (screen router). The simulation lives in src/game (Game.ts, World.ts, GameFactory.ts, traits, locomotors, orders, triggers, superweapons, rules/). The bridge from game objects to visuals is src/engine/renderable (RenderableManager, RenderableFactory, entity/Building|Vehicle|Infantry|Aircraft|Projectile|Anim|Debris...). Low-level graphics are in src/engine/gfx. The UI uses a custom JSX-to-three UI layer (src/gui/jsx, UiScene.ts) plus React DOM components.
Renderer: src/engine/gfx/Renderer.ts wraps a single THREE.WebGLRenderer (three r183, WebGL2). Settings: autoClear off, shadowMap on, NoToneMapping, SRGB output. There is no setPixelRatio or devicePixelRatio handling anywhere, so a Retina display renders at CSS-pixel resolution. Several scenes (world, UI) are rendered one after another, each with its own viewport. No post-processing and no render targets.
Camera: src/engine/renderable/WorldScene.ts uses a THREE.OrthographicCamera rotated by Coords.ISO_CAMERA_ALPHA/BETA. This is a true 3D world viewed isometrically, not 2D blitting. It has an ambient light and one directional light with optional shadow maps (1024×multiplier, ShadowQuality option).
Palettes: every SHP/TMP pixel is kept as an 8-bit palette index in the texture's alpha or red channel. src/engine/gfx/material/paletteShaderLib.ts looks colors up in a palette texture. Each row of that texture is a palette, and house-color remaps are extra rows chosen per instance or per vertex (instancePaletteOffset, vertexPaletteOffset). Palette textures are built in src/engine/gfx/TextureUtils.ts (NearestFilter).
Materials: PaletteBasicMaterial, PaletteLambertMaterial and PalettePhongMaterial are made by string-replacing THREE.ShaderLib basic/lambert/phong GLSL chunks. They are GLSL-only, so moving to WebGPU or TSL would mean rewriting them. Per-object "extraLight" and per-tile tint come from src/engine/Lighting.ts (map [Lighting] ambient/level/tint, tile lights) and gfx/lighting/LightingDirector.ts (nuke and lightning-storm flashes).
SHP: data/ShpFile.ts and ShpImage.ts decode the format. engine/renderable/builder/ShpBuilder.ts, BatchShpBuilder.ts and ShpTextureAtlas.ts pack frames into atlases and draw camera-facing quads with depth. ImageFinder.ts resolves art names to files (theater/new-theater logic).
TMP terrain: data/TmpFile.ts feeds gfx/drawable/TmpDrawable.ts, which packs a TextureAtlas. engine/renderable/entity/map/MapTileLayer.ts merges all tile quads into one mesh, with a per-vertex color multiplier for lighting. Water is ordinary animated TMP/SHP art, with no water shader.
VXL/HVA: data/VxlFile.ts, HvaFile.ts and vxl/normals.ts decode voxels. They are meshed in engine/renderable/builder/vxlGeometry/ (Naive, Culled, Monotone greedy mesher) and turned into three meshes by VxlBatchedBuilder/VxlNonBatchedBuilder (Phong or Lambert palette material). These are real 3D meshes, not pre-rendered sprites.
Instancing bug (INFERENCE, likely): Renderer.supportsInstancing() checks the WebGL1 extension 'ANGLE_instanced_arrays', which a WebGL2 context does not expose. Under r183 instancing therefore probably turns itself off.
Archives and text: MIX via data/MixFile.ts with Blowfish (data/encoding/Blowfish*.ts); CSF via data/CsfFile.ts; INI via data/IniParser.ts and IniFile.ts; maps via data/MapFile.ts; plus Format80/Format5/Format3 and LZO codecs.
Other systems: particles via SPE (DamageSmokeFx, TrailerSmokeFx). Effects in engine/renderable/fx (Tesla, Laser, RadBeam, MindControl link, etc.) and fx/handler (WarheadDetonate, SuperWeapon, Chrono, Crate). Audio via engine/sound (WebAudio, AudioSystem, WorldSound, Music, audio.bag/idx). Video: only the menu BIK (ra2ts_l.bik) is converted to WebM by ffmpeg.wasm (engine/gameRes/VideoConverter.ts). Netcode: deterministic lockstep (GameTurnManager, Prng) with SoloPlayTurnManager, ReplayTurnManager and LanLockstepTurnManager. LAN is a WebRTC data-channel mesh set up by manually exchanging SDP or scanning QR codes (network/lan/*). WOL online is stubbed (network/WolConnection.ts is 3 lines).

feature_completeness:

- Allied campaign: [missing]. No campaign or mission screens, and no TeamTypes, ScriptTypes or Reinforcement system, which campaigns need.
- Soviet campaign: [missing], same reason.
- Yuri's Revenge: [missing]. Engine.getActiveEngine() always returns EngineType.RedAlert2. Some YR mix loading code exists in data/vfs/VirtualFileSystem.ts but nothing calls it. The importer only asks for ra2.mix, language.mix, multi.mix and theme.mix. .yrm maps are not accepted (Engine.supportedMapTypes = ["mpr","map"]).
- Skirmish vs AI: [code]. SkirmishScreen and GameLoader exist. The AI is a TypeScript port of Supalosa's community bot (game/ai/thirdpartbot/builtIn, about 6.1k lines, unlicensed upstream) plus a third-party bot upload sandbox. There is no ai.ini TeamType-based AI. game/ai/Ai.ts is a 9-line stub. AI strength is not verified; the PR history mentions fixes like "AI MCV blocked" and "keep attacking".

asset_requirements:
VERIFIED in src/engine/gameRes/GameResImporter.ts. The user must supply these original RA2 (not YR) files: ra2.mix (expected 281,895,456 bytes), language.mix (53,116,040), multi.mix (25,856,283), and optionally theme.mix (76,862,662, used for music) plus a Taunts folder. They can be provided in three ways:
(a) Pick the game folder with the File System Access API (Chrome/Edge recommended; the README asks for Chrome/Edge with WebGL, WebAudio and FS Access).
(b) Drop or select an archive (.7z/.zip etc.), which is extracted by 7z-wasm.
(c) Enter an archive URL. The default is gameResArchiveUrl=https://download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z, a third-party-hosted pack of EA assets. Using it has its own legal problems; the user should use their own copy, e.g. the EA/Origin/Steam C&C Ultimate Collection.
Files are copied into browser storage (OPFS). language.mix's ra2ts_l.bik is converted to WebM with ffmpeg.wasm, and theme.mix music is extracted. A CDN mode (gameresBaseUrl=/cdn/game-res/v2/) exists, but public/cdn/ is gitignored and empty. The repo itself already ships EA/CD-derived data: public/ini.mix (1.1 MB, original INIs), public/general.csf (RA2 string table), public/res/ra2cd.mix. Custom maps go into a /maps folder in storage.
hd_extensibility:
These notes are about technical feasibility only. The architecture is actually friendly to an HD 2.5D upgrade because it is a real three.js 3D scene with an ortho-iso camera, depth testing and shadow maps. Difficulty estimates are INFERENCE.
1) Hi-res sprite replacement (SHP/TMP → AI-upscaled RGBA with a house-color mask). Hook ImageFinder.find/getFilename (src/engine/ImageFinder.ts) or the image map built in GameLoader.prepareTextures (src/gui/screen/game/GameLoader.ts) so a manifest can supply HD variants. Then add an RGBA path next to the palette path: new materials alongside src/engine/gfx/material/PaletteBasicMaterial.ts, and changes to src/engine/renderable/builder/ShpBuilder.ts, BatchShpBuilder.ts, ShpTextureAtlas.ts and gfx/TextureAtlas.ts (atlas size limits at 2–4× scale). Keep palette-index semantics for remap by storing a remap mask channel and tinting with the house color in the shader (paletteShaderLib.paletteColorFrag). Keep quad world size constant while raising texel density. Terrain goes through engine/renderable/entity/map/MapTileLayer.ts and gfx/drawable/TmpDrawable.ts. Medium–hard, mainly a large asset pipeline plus animation-frame consistency.
2) Voxels. VXL is already meshed in engine/renderable/builder/vxlGeometry/VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder.ts and Culled/Naive, and used in VxlBatchedBuilder/VxlNonBatchedBuilder with PalettePhongMaterial. Options: smooth normals using data/vxl/normals.ts, or a per-unit override registry that loads glTF meshes (hand-made or AI-assisted) in VxlBuilderFactory.ts while keeping HVA animation and turret offsets. Medium.
3) Normal and depth-map lighting for sprites. Add normal-map and height-map textures to the HD sprite atlas and a lit sprite material using the existing directional and ambient lights in WorldScene.ts and the tint and extraLight from engine/Lighting.ts. Sprites are already depth-tested, and ShpBuilder has depth and depthOffset parameters. Medium–hard.
4) Post-processing (bloom, color grading, SSAO-like AO, TAA/FXAA, heat distortion). Insert it in src/engine/gfx/Renderer.ts render(): render the world scene into a WebGLRenderTarget, run EffectComposer passes, then draw the UI scene last. Also add setPixelRatio(devicePixelRatio) for Retina 3456×2234 and fix supportsInstancing() for WebGL2. Easy–medium.
5) Water shader. Classify water tiles from TileSets or theater INI in MapTileLayer.ts and draw a separate water plane mesh with a custom ShaderMaterial (normal-mapped waves, reflection of sky or env, shoreline foam from a distance field of land tiles, wakes for naval units from Vehicle.ts). Medium.
6) Weather. Add a new Renderable layer in WorldScene or MapRenderable (engine/renderable/entity/map/MapRenderable.ts) for GPU rain and snow, fog volumes, and wet-surface darkening through Lighting.applyAmbientOverride. LightningStormFx and NukeLightingFx in engine/gfx/lighting show how lighting overrides work. Medium.
7) GPU particles, explosions and impacts. Currently SPE (old, globally patched: engine/renderable/fx/speCompat.ts, speRuntime.ts) in DamageSmokeFx and TrailerSmokeFx. Explosions are SHP Anim instances (engine/renderable/entity/Anim.ts) spawned by fx/handler/WarheadDetonateFxHandler.ts. Replace them with custom instanced GPU particle systems (flipbook smoke, sparks, debris, shockwave distortion) keyed by warhead or anim name. Medium.
Caveats: all materials are GLSL ShaderChunk string patches on WebGLRenderer, so a WebGPU/TSL move is a large rewrite (hard). Code quality slows everything down: strict off, about 7k `any`, minified remnants, almost no tests.
risks: LEGAL, blocking: the repo's own LICENSE (2026-09-03) says the Chrono Divide-derived code is not licensed at all. Building, publishing or distributing a remaster on it has no legal basis without written permission from Chrono Divide's author (Alexandru Ciucă), and it could be taken down at any time.

LEGAL: provenance is a decompile/migration of a proprietary client's extracted JS bundle. The deleted PROJECT_CONTEXT_SUMMARY.md, the bulk-dump commits and the minified leftovers all show this. Any derivative inherits that taint.
LEGAL: the built-in AI is ported from Supalosa/supalosa-chronodivide-bot, which has no license file (all rights reserved by default).

LEGAL: the repo redistributes EA/Westwood-derived data (public/ini.mix with original ART/AI INIs, general.csf string table, ra2cd.mix). The default gameResArchiveUrl points to a third-party full asset pack (download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z).
Contradictory licensing text: the README still claims GPL-3.0 while the LICENSE denies it. Forks such as OpenRA2/RA2Web and DD-Channel/ra2-web still show GPL-3.0.
Scope gap: no campaigns (and no TeamType/ScriptType/Reinforcement systems), no Yuri's Revenge (hard-coded to RA2), no online, no save/load, no FMV, no map editor. Mods menu is a stub.

Code quality: strict:false, about 6,959 'any', about 270 minified '(e, t)' signatures, fully minified VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder, 26 tsc errors in tools, 7 unit tests total. scripts/ and docs/ (regression suite, alignment log) are gitignored and missing.

Performance: no devicePixelRatio support (blurry on Retina), instancing likely disabled on WebGL2 because of the ANGLE_instanced_arrays check (INFERENCE), open issue about lag with many units, single-threaded simulation.
Renderer lock-in: GLSL ShaderChunk-patched materials tied to WebGLRenderer, and the old SPE particle library needs a global THREE plus shader patches.
Bus factor: essentially one maintainer (173 of 207 commits), bursty activity, last code change 2026-06-23.
Online config points to chronodivide.com WOL servers, and a WeChat-account credit appears in CreditsScreen. Issue #39 reported a prompt to follow a WeChat public account when running the game.
score_rationale: Licensing and legality carry the most weight, and here they are close to disqualifying. The repo itself states the code is reconstructed from the proprietary Chrono Divide client and is unlicensed. The git history shows a migration from an extracted JS bundle. It also bundles EA data and an unlicensed third-party bot. Original-gameplay completeness is moderate: vanilla RA2 skirmish, LAN, replays and most mechanics work (about 5/10), but there is no campaign, no YR, no online and no save/load, and those are core to a faithful remaster. Code modifiability is below average (about 4/10): it builds instantly, but strict mode is off, there are about 7k anys, minified remnants and almost no tests. Renderer upgradability is actually good (about 7/10) thanks to the true 3D ortho scene, voxel meshes, shadow maps, a palette shader with remap rows, and one render loop where post-processing can be inserted. Activity is moderate (977 stars, but essentially one maintainer and bursty). With written permission from Chrono Divide's author I would rate its technical value around 6/10. Without it, it should be used only as private study or reference material, not as the base of a published project, hence 2/10.
